video_directives: Pacing is genuinely good — every 2-4s a new beat, transitions are eased cross-dissolves with hold-time, the suture-action micro-beats (gauze pop-ins, X stitches appearing) land rhythmically

Character life is the weak axis: poses/expressions change per scene (worried, exhausted, shivering pale, walking) but within-scene movement is minimal idle — add breathing sway, blink loops, subtle weight shifts to stop cutout feel

Edit flow works: dissolves are motivated by light-beam continuity and the final return to the hook composition (bed + spotlight + character + title card) closes the loop cleanly; keep that mirror-structure discipline

Nurse at right edge is cropped by frame — either pull him fully into frame or let the crop read as intentional
Bed sits center-low leaving a large empty dead zone in the lower third — add floor-level detail or reframe subject higher
Heart-monitor overlay partially overlaps the bed silhouette — add a subtle separation shadow or lift it off the mattress line for cleaner stacking
Fill or crop the empty bottom third (dark floor band under the monitor) — it reads as a dead zone on a 9:16 frame
Add subtle rim-light or color separation where the white bed sheet blends into the dark background on the right edge
Vary palette temperature slightly in mid-ground (wall panel on right is near-invisible) to add depth layers behind the walking figure
The bright figure floating beside the bed reads as a rendering error (no anchor shadow, glow halo ambiguous) — ground it with contact shadow or clear intent (ghost/translucent treatment)
The faint object silhouette in the bottom-left floor area is a muddy dead-zone artifact — either resolve it as a prop or remove it
Light pool hits the bed but the standing figure sits just outside the key light with a strong self-glow; unify the lighting logic so the eye path bed→figure feels intentional
Bottom third (reflection/floor zone) is a large dead zone — either extend the spotlight pool and character lower into it or crop/tighten the frame to kill the empty band
